What to compare

Factor What to check Why it matters
Support width Check the cradle in both orientations Side buttons or camera bumps can shift the device
Tilt stability Tap near each screen edge at useful angles A stand can tip or fold under touch
Charging access Connect the cable in portrait and landscape The lower port is often blocked
Case allowance Measure with the normal case installed Bare-device specifications may be too narrow

Test the current setup first

  • Support width: check the cradle in both orientations. Record what happens before changing another variable.
  • Tilt stability: tap near each screen edge at useful angles. Record what happens before changing another variable.
  • Charging access: connect the cable in portrait and landscape. Record what happens before changing another variable.

The no-purchase checks for phone stand for vertical vs horizontal cost nothing and create a baseline. Compare the tradeoffs

For phone stand for vertical vs horizontal, compare one change at a time. Start with support width: check the cradle in both orientations. Then check tilt stability, because a stand can tip or fold under touch. During the phone stand for vertical vs horizontal comparison, keep the same game, page, room, and device so the result is easier to attribute.

The remaining checks cover charging access and case allowance. The lower port is often blocked. Bare-device specifications may be too narrow.
